title: The bill as a monitoring signal: the spike that means an incident

videos.script: Some incidents customers never feel. A debug level left on. A load test nobody stopped. A stolen key running machines in a region you never use. The service works, and the only thing that moves is the bill. {{bill}} This lesson makes the bill a signal like any other. Two sources give a daily number: the billing export, by service, and the budget's own topic. {{sources}} Then forty-five days of the shop's costs, and a small program that finds the day the spend changed and the service that moved. Twenty dollars a day, all of it logs. That is not a billing question. It is an incident, with a cause. {{spike}} And a warning about every detector built on a recent baseline. After a week, the spike is the new normal. {{normal}} Last, what deserves a page. Most cost signals are tickets. Two are not. {{page}} This is the last lesson. The course ends where it should: with the bill noticing, and a team that hears about it the same day. {{end}}
